subject: math.DS
name: Picard–Lindelöf theorem
statement: For an ordinary differential equation x′ = f(t,x), continuity of f and local Lipschitz continuity in x imply local existence and uniqueness of a solution through each initial condition.

subject: math.DS
name: Peano existence theorem
statement: If f(t,x) is continuous on a neighborhood of an initial point in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the equation x′ = f(t,x) has a solution on some time interval through that point. Uniqueness is not asserted.

subject: math.DS
name: Grönwall's inequality
statement: If a nonnegative continuous function u on [0,T] satisfies u(t) ≤ a + ∫₀ᵗ b(s)u(s) ds with a ≥ 0 and continuous b ≥ 0, then u(t) ≤ a exp(∫₀ᵗ b(s) ds).

subject: math.DS
name: Flow-box theorem
statement: Near any point at which a smooth vector field is nonzero, there are local coordinates in which the vector field is the constant first coordinate vector field. In these coordinates its trajectories are straight coordinate lines.

subject: math.DS
name: Hartman–Grobman theorem
statement: Near a hyperbolic equilibrium of a continuously differentiable autonomous vector field, the nonlinear flow is locally topologically conjugate to the flow of its linearization. Hyperbolicity means that no eigenvalue of the linearization has zero real part.

subject: math.DS
name: Stable manifold theorem
statement: At a hyperbolic equilibrium of a Cʳ vector field, r ≥ 1, there are Cʳ local stable and unstable invariant manifolds tangent to the stable and unstable eigenspaces of the linearization. Points on these manifolds converge to the equilibrium in forward and backward time, respectively.

subject: math.DS
name: Center manifold theorem
statement: Near an equilibrium of a Cʳ finite-dimensional vector field, with finite integer r ≥ 1, there is a local Cʳ invariant center manifold tangent to the generalized eigenspace whose eigenvalues have zero real part. The center manifold need not be unique.

subject: math.DS
name: Lyapunov stability theorem
statement: If an equilibrium of a continuously differentiable autonomous system has a continuously differentiable function V that is positive away from the equilibrium, zero at it, and nonincreasing along trajectories in a neighborhood, the equilibrium is stable. If the derivative of V along trajectories is strictly negative away from the equilibrium, it is asymptotically stable.

subject: math.DS
name: LaSalle invariance principle
statement: Let a locally Lipschitz autonomous system have a compact positively invariant set K and a continuously differentiable function V with derivative along the flow at most zero on K. Every trajectory starting in K approaches the largest invariant subset of the set where that derivative is zero.

subject: math.DS
name: Poincaré–Bendixson theorem
statement: For a continuously differentiable vector field on the plane, a nonempty compact omega-limit set containing no equilibrium is a periodic orbit.

subject: math.DS
name: Hopf bifurcation theorem
statement: Suppose a smooth one-parameter family of vector fields has an equilibrium whose linearization has exactly one simple pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues, with all other eigenvalues off the imaginary axis. If the pair crosses the imaginary axis with nonzero speed and the first Lyapunov coefficient is nonzero, a branch of small periodic orbits bifurcates from the equilibrium.

subject: math.DS
name: Liouville's theorem for Hamiltonian flows
statement: The flow of a smooth Hamiltonian on a 2n-dimensional symplectic manifold preserves its symplectic form and hence its volume form ωⁿ/n!, wherever the flow is defined.

subject: math.DS
name: Poincaré recurrence theorem
statement: If a transformation preserves a finite measure, then for every measurable set A, almost every point of A returns to A infinitely many times under positive iterates.

subject: math.DS
name: Birkhoff ergodic theorem
statement: For a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space and an integrable function f, the time averages of f converge almost everywhere to an invariant integrable function. If the transformation is ergodic, the limit equals the space average ∫f almost everywhere.

subject: math.DS
name: Von Neumann mean ergodic theorem
statement: For a unitary operator U on a Hilbert space, the averages (I + U + ⋯ + Uⁿ⁻¹)/n converge strongly to the orthogonal projection onto the subspace fixed by U.

subject: math.DS
name: Krylov–Bogolyubov theorem
statement: Every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact metric space preserves at least one Borel probability measure.

subject: math.DS
name: Oseledets multiplicative ergodic theorem
statement: Let an invertible ergodic probability-preserving transformation carry a measurable invertible finite-dimensional matrix cocycle with integrable log⁺ norms of both the matrix and its inverse. Almost everywhere, the vector space has an invariant splitting into subspaces on which the exponential growth rates are well-defined constant Lyapunov exponents.

subject: math.DS
name: Pesin entropy formula
statement: For a C¹⁺ᵅ diffeomorphism, α > 0, of a closed Riemannian manifold preserving a probability measure absolutely continuous with respect to volume, the measure-theoretic entropy equals the integral of the sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents, counted with multiplicity.

subject: math.DS
name: Sharkovsky's theorem: period-three consequence
statement: If a continuous self-map of a real interval has a point of least period three, it has a point of every positive integer least period.

subject: math.DS
name: Hyperbolic shadowing lemma
statement: For a compact hyperbolic invariant set of a C¹ diffeomorphism of a compact manifold, every sufficiently accurate bi-infinite pseudo-orbit in the set is uniformly approximated by a true orbit. If the hyperbolic set is locally maximal, the shadowing orbit can be chosen inside it.
